neighbours.label: adjective that rates how an experience or situation feels to live through (peaceful, miserable, easy, exhausting)
fire: After the long war, the villagers finally enjoyed a calm summer by the lake.
Waiting three hours in the cold rain was a painful experience for the fans.
Most guests found the boat trip pleasant and relaxing.
The first winter in the new country was lonely and difficult for the family.
Moving house with two toddlers turned out to be surprisingly stressful.
She said the hike back down the mountain was a gentle and soothing walk.
For the prisoners, life in the camp was grim and hopeless.
Thanks to the new software, filing taxes felt simple this year.
quiet: After the long war, the villagers finally held a census by the lake.
Waiting three hours in the cold rain was a recent change for the fans.
Most guests found the boat trip short and well organised.
The first winter in the new country was recorded in the family diary.
Moving house with two toddlers turned out to be surprisingly common.
She said the hike back down the mountain was a long and steep walk.
For the prisoners, life in the camp was regulated by strict timetables.
Thanks to the new software, filing taxes was digital this year.

predictions: Fire on felt-quality adjectives (calm, painful, pleasant, hard) describing an experience; near misses use neutral descriptive adjectives (quick, common, large, recent) in the same frames.
notes: Card: ' including' x8 (license boilerplate) plus peaceful, unpleasant, miserable, exhausting, easy.
